newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks end on strong gains, HSBC leads.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks end on strong gains, HSBC leads.

text.p: A record-setting performance by HSBC Holdings led Hong Kong shares to a strong close on Tuesday and keen interest continued to drive China-related shares.
The Hang Seng Index closed 144.57 points, or 1.08 percent, higher at 13,520.26. Turnover was HK$9.69 billion compared with HK$8.80 billion on Monday.
"Investors generally expect March will be very good, so they will try to bargain-hunt," said Peter So, deputy head of research at Schroder Securities.
Hong Kong's major blue chips will be reporting corporate results in March, starting with HSBC Holdings on Monday.
The market generally expects strong earnings growth from the banking giant. Its shares rose HK$5.00 to HK$193.50 after reaching an all-time high of HK$194.00 during the session.
On Monday, HSBC's indirectly wholly-owned unit Hong Kong Bank of Canada posted a 28 percent rise in net profit to C$31.0 million for the first quarter ended January 31.
"After the release of the results of Hong Kong Bank of Canada, investors generally believe that the other overseas countries should perform just as impressively," said So.
H-shares also put on a strong performance on Tuesday, rising 8.24 points, or 0.85 percent, to 982.15.
"Basically it is just a rebound and people are becoming more optimistic about China in the future," said Kelvin Tang, an analyst at ImPac Asset Management.

Edwin Cheung, dealing director at Taiwan Securities, said investors were encouraged that Chinese President Jiang Zemin had vowed in his eulogy for deceased patriarch Deng Xiaoping to push ahead with market-oriented reforms.
"This morning Beijing reiterated the open-door policy will still be maintained," said Cheung
A funeral service for Deng, who died last Wednesday, was held in Beijing's Great Hall of the People on Tuesday.
"The H-shares were under consolidation before the death of Deng Xiaoping," said So.
He said earnings prospects for the Hong Kong-listed mainland firms should improve this year after a poor performance in 1996.
Among the red chip favourites, CITIC Pacific rose HK$0.20 to HK$39.60 and China Resources gained HK$0.35 to HK$16.95.
In the property sector, Cheung Kong jumped HK$1.50 to HK$73.25, Sun Hung Kai Properties gained HK$0.25 to HK$89.75 and Henderson Land rose HK$0.50 to HK$70.00.
